title: Living With High Prices in Rural Virginia
summary:
Java Jacks is a cafe in Tappahannock, Virginia, owned by Jeans Owens. She took over the cafe eight years ago with her husband.

Since 2022, prices have gone up a lot. Coffee at the cafe costs more than 30 percent more. A takeout box that once cost 12 cents now costs nearly 30 cents, and a cup with lid and straw that once cost 3 cents now costs more than 20 cents. The power bill went from about $450 or $500 a month to more than $1,000.

Owens keeps some meals at $10 to stay cheap. She buys milk and juice at Walmart instead of from a supplier, and checks three suppliers to pick the cheapest one.

Finding workers is her hardest problem. She helps workers find homes and drives five of them to work.

Jameka Campbell has two jobs and two children. She works at Menokin and for a food-growing group. She uses Walgreens coupons and tries to spend $100 a month on home supplies. "I'm not rich. I'm not poor. I'm in between," she said.
why_it_matters: When prices rise, families and small shops have to make careful choices about what to buy.

background_read: Small cafes buy food, cups and power to serve customers.
When the prices of those things go up, the cafe must charge more or find cheaper ways to buy.
In small towns, there may be few shops and few workers, so owners must be creative.

WHAT: They are dealing with rising prices in a small Virginia town
